sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. sample of marked blind two-replicate observations \(O_i=(Y_i,X_i,S_{i1},S_{i2})\).
sampling_model.units: Superpopulation units have finite-stratum \(X_i\), compact latent dose \(A_i\), and bounded potential-outcome schedules generated simultaneously as \(Y_i(a)=h(a,X_i,V_i)\) by a jointly measurable response surface, with \(V_i\perp A_i\mid X_i\); the stratum-specific causal means are continuous on \(I\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\), with independent errors that need not be identically distributed or symmetric and may have spectral gaps. The class fixes \(q_e>1\) and \(E|U_j|^{q_e}\le M_e\), and only \(E[U_2]=0\) fixes location. The moment bound implies \( |\phi_j(t)|\ge1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e}\), so \(\nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\) and \(c_*=1/2\) give a common protected neighborhood rather than an additional model restriction.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The explicit conservative procedure uses relaxed order-\(d\) B-spline families for \(f_x,q_x\), finite atomic error laws satisfying the \(q_e\)-moment and centering restrictions and the moment-derived protected-neighborhood bounds, and \(p_x\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) against simultaneous empirical probability- and marked-channel restrictions on \(\mathcal D_n\); its outer splines are feasibility devices rather than asserted model laws. A second, abstract procedure profiles the same empirical radii with no approximation allowances over the exact compact projected class \(\mathscr K\), then takes clipped extrema of \(\mu_{\vartheta}\). The latter is an infinite-dimensional existence construction and is not claimed to be computationally implementable.

body.tldr: This is a statistical-inference paper about a causal ADRF under two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates. The fixed quantitative class now allows every \(\beta>1/2\) and every fixed \(q_e>1\); the common moment bound itself supplies a uniform protected frequency neighborhood, so no separate local spectral-modulus restriction is assumed. Analytic cocycle identification and an explicit structural response-surface condition establish the causal identifying functional. Two simultaneous bands are distinguished: an explicit finite relaxed outer-sieve construction is uniformly honest and clipped to \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), while an abstract noncomputational exact-class construction is uniformly honest with uniformly \(o(1)\) expected maximal width. Neither construction proves the candidate \(r_n\) rate. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli lower modulus remains unresolved, so there is no matched honest-band rate.

project_justification.gap: Existing statistical results cover blind repeated-measurement density estimation, confidence bands under auxiliary-error, symmetric-error, or fixed-operator designs, and pointwise continuous-treatment inference. They do not provide a quantitative shrinking rate for a uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band with blind nonidentical asymmetric replicate errors and possible spectral gaps. The present empirical-grid outer set lacks a quantitative marked inverse modulus, and the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus needed for a sharp all-band converse remains unproved.
project_justification.niche: The inferential niche is a nonlinear severe inverse problem over the full Sobolev-continuity range \(\beta>1/2\). Compact treatment support supplies entire transforms, one centered replicate fixes translation, and the uniform \(q_e>1\) moment bound yields \( |\phi_Q(t)|\ge1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e}\), hence a common near-origin conditioning region without a separate spectral assumption. The causal target is a stratum-weighted quotient. A jointly measurable response surface driven by an exogenous random element and continuity of the stratum-specific causal mean bridge that observed regression quotient to the point-dose causal curve. The distinction between qualitative identification and quantitative confidence-set diameter is essential here.
project_justification.fill: The paper delivers two inference maps over this enlarged class. The explicit map uses deterministic spline, frequency, truncation, and atomic dimensions; simultaneous probability-, marked-, and mass-channel radii; relaxed compact outer signal sieves; moment-constrained error sieves with the derived protected neighborhood; a joint feasible set; and measurable clipped ADRF extrema. It proves uniform simultaneous coverage and \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), but no shrinkage. In parallel, exact empirical-channel residuals are profiled over a compact projected nuisance class with no separately imposed local-modulus constraint. Compactness, expanding-grid equality, and marked cocycle injectivity prove that this abstract exact-class band is uniformly honest and has uniformly \(o(1)\) expected maximal width. The qualitative argument supplies no explicit modulus, and the sharp \(O(r_n)\) upper and matching marked converse remain open.

body.related_work: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy provide the unmarked probability-channel cocycle, constrained polynomial estimator, and compact-support \(L^2\) minimax experiment that inform the analytic machinery. Their qualitative H1--H2 identification class has no common error-moment radius and identifies only up to translation; their estimation classes add separate quantitative restrictions, and their Theorem 4 is a latent-density \(L^2\) converse rather than an ADRF-band converse. In the present class, the sole uniform error restriction beyond independence and centering is a fixed \(q_e>1\) moment radius, from which the protected neighborhood is derived. Their rate argument uses a protected-region integrated contrast with nearly parametric forward error and does not supply a Lipschitz inverse for the present grid set whose tolerance contains polynomial Jackson error. Gassiat, Le Corff, and Lehéricy supply the broader analytic-continuation principle for blind deconvolution. Huang and Zhang formulate the error-contaminated continuous-treatment ADRF and derive pointwise inference with a known everywhere-nonzero error transform. Kato and Sasaki (2018) develop deconvolution bands with an unknown error distribution using an auxiliary error sample, together with a symmetric-error repeated-measurement route; that design differs from two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates and has neither the marked quotient nor joint cell-mass profiling. Kato and Sasaki (2019) obtain multiplier-bootstrap uniform bands under conventional spectral conditions. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura invert Kotlarski restrictions to retain coverage without completeness, but do not establish a shrinking marked-quotient band here. Babii studies honest expected diameter for fixed linear inverse operators. Low supplies a testing-to-expected-length reduction only after a marked modulus is established. None of these sources proves the missing quantitative diameter or fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus for the present problem.
body.interpretation: The observed two-channel law identifies the continuous regression curve \(q_x/f_x\). The common near-zero nonvanishing region used by the cocycle is a consequence of the uniform \(q_e>1\) moment bound, not a separate spectral restriction; open zero sets away from that region remain allowed. Structural exogeneity first equates the regression curve with the stratum-specific causal mean almost everywhere in dose; positivity and continuity then extend the equality to every target dose. Coordinatewise weak unconfoundedness and almost-sure consistency alone would not suffice because they permit treatment-dependent diagonal modifications on null sets.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The causal bridge, moment-derived protected neighborhood, analytic-cocycle identification, simultaneous transform concentration, uniform Jackson approximation for every \(\beta>1/2\), relaxed outer-sieve embedding, and clipped uniform coverage are established. The finite grid-sieve set has no quantitative inverse modulus and therefore no shrinking-width guarantee. Exact-class compactness over the \(q_e>1\) moment class yields a separate uniformly honest band with uniformly \(o(1)\) expected width, but gives no rate, tuning law, or finite algorithm. The sharp-rate program still requires a protected-cube analytic-polynomial confidence construction for both probability and signed marked channels. On the lower side, compatible strict-interior fixed nuisances, a Bernoulli-range Sobolev packet, and a weighted Hellinger or chi-square conversion remain unresolved; the former independently specified \(c_0=1\) obstruction has disappeared with deletion of the separate local-modulus assumption.
body.honest_scope: The enlarged fixed quantitative model has compact dose support, bounded outcomes, Sobolev radii with \(\beta>1/2\), overlap, finite-stratum positivity, a fixed \(q_e>1\) error-moment radius, centering of the second error, and the structural causal response surface. It imposes no separate local spectral-modulus restriction: \(\nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\) and \(c_*=1/2\) follow uniformly from the moment bound. The explicit finite relaxed outer-sieve band is uniformly honest for all sufficiently large \(n\) and universally clipped to width at most \(2B_Y\), with no proved shrinkage. The parallel exact-class band is abstract and noncomputational; it is uniformly honest and its expected maximal width is uniformly \(o(1)\), but no explicit rate follows. In particular, no \(O(r_n)\), minimax-matching, or rate-elbow claim is made. The matching-converse kernel remains open as \(\mathrm{oeq{:}fixed\text{-}nuisance\text{-}marked\text{-}modulus}\).
